transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Liam Patel (Redwood AE), Sofia Morales (Redwood SE), Dr. Emily Hart (Sunnyside Head of IT), Marcus Lee (Security Architect), Priya Nair (Director of AI)

Summary (auto):
Redwood and Sunnyside scoped a security-focused POC to validate functional performance and compliance posture. Primary concerns: SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO with SAML integration, RBAC and audit logs, KMS/encryption, and data residency. Discussed workload sizing, test benchmarks (p95 latency, token throughput), and a 2-4 week pilot timeline. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send security artifacts, schedule benchmark run, customer to provide anonymized test data and success criteria.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Liam Patel: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this to about 45 minutes and then I'll -- uh -- leave time for questions. Sofia and I are from Redwood, we're the AE/SE pair on this.
[00:14] Dr. Emily Hart: Thanks Liam. Quick context, we're a midsize clinic network, about 22 clinics, and we want to pilot LLM-powered triage and notes summarization. Security is the gating factor for us, so today's about making sure the pilot meets compliance.
[00:29] Sofia Morales: Got it. We'll focus on the security checklist and then the POC sizing/benchmarks. Marcus, maybe you can start with the high level of requirements?
[00:38] Marcus Lee: Sure. SOC 2 Type II evidence first, ISO27001 would be a plus. We require SSO with SAML, enterprise RBAC, immutable audit logs, and customer-managed keys (KMS) if possible. Also data residency for PHI - likely must stay in us-east-1. And for the pilot we need logging retention for at least 90 days.
[00:56] Sofia Morales: Okay, that's clear. Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 at the org level, we can share the reports and a compliance package. For KMS we support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated - for Hosted we have BYOK options via KMS integrations. Audit logs and RBAC are available through the Console; we can export logs to your SIEM.
[01:12] Marcus Lee: When you say export, is that push to our Splunk or pull? We need server-to-server ingest.
[01:18] Liam Patel: We support push via secure forwarder or S3 export hooks that your SIEM can pull from; we can set up a secure delivery with IAM roles. We'll include the log export options in the security package.
[01:28] Priya Nair: From the AI side, success criteria are: 1) summary F1 score above our baseline on 2k notes, 2) p95 latency under 700ms for the small-note workflow, 3) accuracy regressions less than 2% compared to current rule-based baseline. Timeline-wise we want a 3-week pilot with a one-week buffer.
[01:45] Sofia Morales: Perfect. For the p95 latency target, does that assume cached prefixes and batching disabled? Or do you expect batching?
[01:52] Priya Nair: For triage we want low latency so minimal batching; for nightly bulk summaries we can batch. So pilot should test both low-latency (single request) and high-throughput (batch) paths.
[02:03] Sofia Morales: Makes sense. For sizing, can you give rough QPS and token sizes?
[02:08] Dr. Emily Hart: Average payload is 350 tokens, peak QPS around 5 for triage, batch jobs run overnight at ~200 reqs/min with average 1,200 tokens per request. For the pilot we'll send an anonymized subset ~5k requests.
[02:24] Liam Patel: Good, that gives us a baseline. Our POC plan: run targeted benchmarks against a verified model variant, with KV cache enabled for prefix reuse. We'll do a low-latency run (single-shot, cache warm) and a throughput run (concurrent workers, batching). We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and token/sec and cost estimates.
[02:41] Marcus Lee: On encryption, we need clarification on data at rest for logs and retained prompts. Can logs include redacted content? We prefer redaction before export.
[02:49] Sofia Morales: We can redact at the client side prior to sending, and we also support server-side redact hooks for certain PII patterns. For logs retention we can configure retention policies per route and per team.
[03:00] Dr. Emily Hart: What about the authentication flow? We use Okta, want SSO via SAML and SCIM for user provisioning, and enforce 2FA.
[03:08] Liam Patel: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC integrates with SAML groups, and admin roles can be mapped. MFA enforcement is typically via your IdP (Okta). We'll include a sample SAML integration doc.
[03:18] Priya Nair: For auditability we need immutable logs tied to user identity and the ability to export per-request metadata including model id, prompt hash, latency, and token counts.
[03:27] Sofia Morales: The Console records per-request metadata; we can produce audit exports that include model id, request id, user, route, prompt length, token counts, and latency. Exports can be sent to your S3 or SIEM.
[03:38] Marcus Lee: Can we get read-only access for our security team to the Console during the pilot?
[03:42] Liam Patel: Yes. We'll provision RBAC roles - read-only security auditor role that limits access to logs and audit exports.
[03:48] Dr. Emily Hart: About private deployment vs hosted - our default is to try Hosted with BYOK, but if the compliance review flags issues, we want a Dedicated or Private option. What's the delta in setup time and cost?
[03:58] Sofia Morales: Hosted + BYOK is fastest - we can onboard in a few days once contracts and SSO are done. Dedicated (reserved capacity) takes 2-4 weeks to provision and includes SLA guarantees. Private (VPC/on-prem) is the longest - typically 6-8 weeks. We'll include cost ranges in the follow-up SOW.
[04:17] Priya Nair: For the benchmark, will you run on the same hardware we'll get in Dedicated? We need representative results.
[04:22] Sofia Morales: We'll run benchmarks on the model variant mapped to your prospective Dedicated profile. We can also do an on-prem-like run if you want Private-level parity - that requires more setup.
[04:30] Liam Patel: Quick note on model selection: for PHI we recommend using the curated open models we've validated plus quantized variants for cost control. We'll document the model catalog and performance profiles.
[04:39] Dr. Emily Hart: Any competitor gaps we should be aware of? Marcus: we evaluated Anthropic and OpenAI; Anthropic had good safety tooling but limited VPC options, OpenAI had good performance but we couldn't get compliant log export without enterprise contract.
[04:53] Sofia Morales: Understood. We'll highlight the differences in the security package.
[04:57] Priya Nair: Next, timeline: if we get the docs this week, can we kick benchmarks next Tuesday and have results the following week?
[05:04] Liam Patel: Yes, proposed timeline: send docs by 2027-06-16, customer provides data by 2027-06-17, benchmark run 2027-06-20, results review 2027-06-24. That fits a 3-week pilot window.
[05:15] Marcus Lee: One more question - can audit logs be tamper-evident? We want a chain of custody for requests.
[05:21] Sofia Morales: We provide cryptographic integrity checks on exports and can include signed manifests for exports to your S3. For higher assurance, Dedicated/Private options allow you to control keying material.
[05:30] Dr. Emily Hart: That should work.
[05:33] Liam Patel: Great. I'll recap the action items and owners at the end. Any last questions?
[05:38] Priya Nair: Nothing here. Marcus?
[05:40] Marcus Lee: No, thanks. We'll review the package when you send it.
[05:42] Liam Patel: Perfect, thanks everyone. We'll send the SOC2/ISO pack, SAML sample, RBAC mapping guide, and benchmark plan. Follow-up meeting invite for 2027-06-24 to review.

Recap / Next Steps (auto):
- Redwood to send SOC 2 Type II report, ISO27001 summary, security package and SAML/SCIM docs (Liam)
- Redwood to prepare benchmark plan and run against Dedicated-equivalent model variant (Sofia)
- Sunnyside to provide anonymized test set and define pass/fail success criteria (Priya)
- Schedule results review meeting for 2027-06-24

References shared: security-package.pdf (link in chat), benchmark-plan.xlsx (link), sample-saml-config.md (link)
